text:
jordan: quick q — we've been getting requests to add more telemetry for console queries, but i'm worried about RBAC leaks and perf. thoughts on where to sample/log?

emily: expanding telemetry sounds great for observability, but yeah we can't accidentally log row-level authz or PII. we should separate metrics from logs.

sam: agree. two quick constraints: (1) sampling should not increase request latency (no sync disk writes on hot path), (2) authz filters must never be materialized in plain text into logs.

jordan: proposed options: sample at routing layer (cheap, before authz), sample after authz (lowers risk but needs careful scrub), or do event-driven async sampling from the console proxy.

taylor: routing-layer sampling = best for perf but we lose info about final query shape after panel projection. for anomaly detection we need the post-projection shape.

emily: from product POV we want per-panel failure/latency/QL metrics and a small sample of post-projection queries for debugging. not full traces for every request.

sam: what if we do hybrid: lightweight counters at routing layer + a bounded async sampler that pulls post-authz query payloads into a sidecar queue for scrubbing and enrichment before they hit logs/metrics pipeline.

jordan: sketch of flow:
```
client -> edge -> router (increment counters) -> authz -> projection -> sidecar enqueue (sampled) -> scrub + enrich -> long-term telemetry
```

jordan: scrub rules: remove tenant_id, replace user ids with hash, strip specific filter values, redact literal values > 100 chars. store sampling metadata: sample_rate, reason_tag, routing_node.

taylor: agree on scrub rules. also need to ensure sampling respects tenant level config/opt-outs and enterprise privacy contracts.

emily: add a product flag to enable richer samples per workspace for enterprise customers (billing+support). default off for general accounts.

sam: we need an SLO note: sidecar enqueue must be best-effort. if queue full -> drop samples (emit sample_drop metric). do not block main request.

jordan: implementation concerns: backpressure, queue size per-tenant, and how to tie a sample back to trace/span without exposing authz. maybe attach opaque sample_id that maps in internal store.

taylor: operationally we should route sampled payloads to a private telemetry pipeline (long retention only for enterprise opt-in). open-source/hosted defaults to short retention and strict scrubbing.

emily: UX: console should show "sampled request ID" in the panel debug view, but only for users with permission; that ID hits an internal lookup endpoint.

sam: security review item: ensure scrubber can't be bypassed if a new panel projection changes shape. add unit tests that assert no authz tokens appear in sampled payloads.

jordan: quick config idea for sampling rate per-*layers* as YAML:
```yaml
sampling:
  router_rate: 0.05  # counters only
  post_projection_rate: 0.005  # full payload to scrubber
  enterprise_overrides:
    workspace_123: 0.2
```

jordan: action items: (1) taylor to prototype sidecar enqueue + scrubber (2) sam to draft security testcases and queue backpressure policy (3) emily to spec enterprise opt-in UX + billing implications.

taylor: i'll start the prototype this week, will put an initial PR behind feature flag.

sam: i'll write the tests and add gate checks to the CI. also will add a SLO for sample pipeline ingestion latency.

emily: i'll write the product spec and short email to legal for privacy confirmation.

ops-bot: deploy 1959990123 to console-proxy succeeded :white_check_mark: (sha=abcd1234)

jordan: cool — let's sync Wed 11am to review the prototype and security checklist. thanks all :thumbsup:
